figures.name: Abraham
figures.who: herdsman of Ur and Haran, called out to Canaan

pace.did: He went from Haran when he was told to go, and Lot went with him.
He rose early in the morning, saddled his donkey and set out for the place he had been told of.
pace.quote: Abraham rose early in the morning, and saddled his donkey

voice.did: He came near and put his objection about Sodom to God out loud.
He asked once more, about ten, saying he would speak just this once more.

lead.did: He led out three hundred and eighteen of his own men, pursued as far as Dan and brought back Lot and the goods.
He told Lot to choose a direction and said he would take the other.

conflict.did: He proposed a separation to Lot to end the quarrel between their herdsmen.
conflict.quote: Please, let there be no strife between you and me

conflict.did: He came near and argued for Sodom, asking whether the Judge of all the earth would destroy the righteous with the wicked.

doubt.did: He asked for something to go on before accepting the promise of the land.
doubt.quote: Lord GOD, how will I know that I will inherit it?

doubt.did: He fell on his face and laughed, asking whether a hundred-year-old man would have a child.

plan.did: He split the wood for the offering and saddled the donkey before leaving.
He went up with the fire and the wood and no lamb, and told Isaac that God would provide the lamb.

figures.name: Moses
figures.who: raised in Pharaoh's house, shepherd in Midian, leader of Israel out of Egypt

pace.did: He looked both ways, killed the Egyptian he had seen striking a Hebrew and hid the body in the sand.
At the bush he asked that someone else be sent.
pace.quote: Oh, Lord, please send someone else.

voice.did: He answered his sending by asking who he was to go to Pharaoh.
voice.quote: Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh

voice.did: He begged the LORD and asked out loud why His wrath burnt hot against His people.

lead.did: He and Aaron went to Pharaoh with the demand to let the people go.
He chose able men, made them rulers over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens, and let them judge the small cases.

conflict.did: He and Aaron carried the demand to Pharaoh to his face.
He threw down the tablets, burnt the calf, ground it to powder and made the people drink it.
He begged the LORD, asking why His wrath burnt hot against the people He had brought out of Egypt.

doubt.did: He said the people would not believe him and would say the LORD had not appeared to him.
He asked how flocks and herds or all the fish of the sea could feed six hundred thousand men for a month.

plan.did: He set up a standing order of rulers so that cases were judged at all times and only hard ones came to him.

figures.name: Joseph
figures.who: eleventh son of Jacob, sold into Egypt, then set over its grain

pace.did: He set out a scheme of appointment and storage across the seven plenteous years against the seven of famine before anything was done.
He recognised his brothers and dealt with them as a stranger instead of saying who he was.
pace.quote: acted like a stranger to them, and spoke roughly with them

voice.did: He recognised his brothers and acted like a stranger to them instead of telling them who he was.
He turned away from them to weep, then came back, spoke to them and bound Simeon in front of them.
He told his brothers the dream about their sheaves bowing to his.

lead.did: The keeper of the prison put all the prisoners into his hand, and he was responsible for all that was done there.
He gathered the food of seven years and stored it city by city until he stopped counting.

conflict.did: He told the brothers who had sold him not to be grieved or angry with themselves.
He promised to provide for them and their little ones, and spoke kindly to them.
He took Simeon from among them and bound him before their eyes.

doubt.did: The text does not show this.

plan.did: He proposed taking a fifth of the produce through seven plenteous years against seven years of famine.
He carried the storage out himself, laying up grain in each city from the fields around it.

figures.name: David
figures.who: shepherd of Bethlehem, harpist, outlaw captain, king of Israel

pace.did: He ran towards the Philistine line to meet Goliath.
pace.quote: David hurried and ran towards the army to meet the Philistine

pace.did: He called for the ephod and asked whether to pursue before he went after the raiders.

voice.did: He told Saul that his servant would go and fight the Philistine.
He lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan.

lead.did: Four hundred men in distress, in debt and discontented gathered to him at the cave and he became their captain.
He offered himself to Saul as the one who would go and fight.

conflict.did: He went out to meet the Philistine in single combat and struck him with a stone.
He showed Saul the cut skirt of his robe and said he had not killed him.
He stopped Abishai from striking the sleeping Saul.

doubt.did: He asked whether he would overtake the raiders before setting out after them.
He asked whether to go and strike the Philistines, and asked a second time before he went.
He asked whether to go up against the Philistines and whether they would be given into his hand.
When the child died he got up, washed, worshipped and ate, and said he could not bring him back.

plan.did: He said he would make preparation for the house his son would build, and prepared abundantly before his death.
plan.quote: So David prepared abundantly before his death.

plan.did: He arrived at Nob with nothing and asked for five loaves or whatever was available.
He had come away without his sword or weapons and had to ask what was there.
plan.quote: I haven’t brought my sword or my weapons with me

figures.name: Jonathan
figures.who: eldest son of Saul, soldier, David's covenant friend

pace.did: He told his armour bearer to come over to the Philistine garrison with him, and did not tell his father.
He proposed the crossing on the spot and went.

voice.did: He went over to the garrison without telling his father.
He passed the warning to David through arrows so that even the boy with him knew nothing.
voice.quote: Only Jonathan and David knew the matter.

voice.did: He spoke to Saul directly on David's behalf.

lead.did: He took off his own robe, clothing, sword, bow and sash and gave them to David.
He went out to David in the woods and told him he would be king and that he himself would be next to him.

conflict.did: He put David's case to Saul until Saul swore David would not be put to death.

doubt.did: The text does not show this.

plan.did: He went out into the field at the time appointed with David and shot the arrows for the boy to find.
He went over to the garrison with only the young man who bore his armour.

figures.name: Elijah
figures.who: prophet of Gilead in the days of Ahab

pace.did: When he saw it he arose and ran for his life to Beersheba, and left his servant there.

voice.did: He put the choice to the assembled people out loud.
voice.quote: How long will you waver between the two sides?

voice.did: At noon he mocked the prophets of Baal in front of the crowd.

lead.did: He called all the people over to him and repaired the altar in front of them.
He went over to Elisha at the plough and put his own mantle on him.

conflict.did: He came near to all the people and put the choice between the LORD and Baal to them.
He met Ahab after Naboth's death and told him to his face what he had done.

doubt.did: He asked God why evil had come on the widow he was staying with.
He went to the brook Cherith and lived there as he had been told.

plan.did: At the brook, where he had been told to go, he lived on bread and meat brought to him morning and evening.
plan.quote: The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening

plan.did: Sent on to Zarephath, he came to the city gate and asked a widow gathering sticks for water and a morsel of bread.

figures.name: Nehemiah
figures.who: cupbearer to Artaxerxes, then governor over the rebuilding of Jerusalem's wall

pace.did: On hearing about the wall he sat down, wept and mourned for several days before doing anything.
He was in Jerusalem three days, then rode out at night to inspect the broken walls before saying a word about his plan.

voice.did: He kept his intention for Jerusalem to himself while he surveyed the ground.
voice.quote: I didn’t tell anyone what my God put into my heart to do for Jerusalem

voice.did: The rulers, priests, nobles and workers were still not told where he had been or what he had done.
He called a great assembly and charged the nobles and rulers with usury in front of it.

lead.did: He stationed the people by family with swords, spears and bows and addressed the nobles, rulers and the rest himself.
He split his servants between the work and the weapons and kept the trumpeter beside him.

conflict.did: He contended with the nobles and rulers over what they were charging their brothers.
He contended with the men who had married foreign wives and struck some of them.
conflict.quote: I contended with them, cursed them, struck certain of them, plucked off their hair

conflict.did: He sent messengers to say he was doing a great work and could not come down.

doubt.did: He questioned the men who came from Judah about the survivors and about Jerusalem before acting.
He answered the opposition by saying that they, the servants of God, would arise and build.

plan.did: He set the king a return date and asked in advance for letters to the governors and timber from the king's forest.
He arranged the work so half the men built while half stood armed.

figures.name: Daniel
figures.who: exile of Judah, trained for the Babylonian court, to whom the king's dreams were made known

pace.did: He went in and asked the king to appoint him a time before he would give the interpretation.
He asked the steward for a ten-day test of vegetables and water.

voice.did: He was troubled by the vision and said nothing of it to anyone.
voice.quote: I kept the matter in my heart

voice.did: He told Nebuchadnezzar to his face to break off his sins.
He refused Belshazzar's gifts and read the writing anyway.

lead.did: He went home and told Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah so they would ask for mercy along with him.
He asked the king to put Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego over the affairs of the province.

conflict.did: He offered the steward a ten-day test that could be settled by looking at their faces.
He gave the king counsel the king had not asked for.

doubt.did: He went up to one of those standing by and asked what the vision meant.
When he had seen the vision he sought to understand it.
He said he had heard and had not understood, and asked what the outcome of these things would be.
doubt.quote: I heard, but I didn’t understand.

plan.did: He settled beforehand what he would not eat and then made his request.

figures.name: John the Baptist
figures.who: preacher in the wilderness of Judea who baptised in the Jordan

pace.did: The text does not show this.

voice.did: He said what he thought of the Pharisees and Sadducees to their faces as they came.
voice.quote: You offspring of vipers

voice.did: He told Herod that his marriage to Herodias was not lawful.
voice.quote: It is not lawful for you to have her.

lead.did: He pointed two of his own disciples at Jesus and they left him and followed Jesus.
He said his own part was to become less as the other became greater.
lead.quote: He must increase, but I must decrease.

conflict.did: He challenged the Pharisees and Sadducees who had come out to him.
He told the king to his face that he was in the wrong, and was arrested for it.

doubt.did: From prison he sent two disciples to ask Jesus directly whether He was the one to come.
doubt.quote: Are you he who comes, or should we look for another?

plan.did: The text does not show this.

figures.name: Peter
figures.who: fisherman of Galilee, apostle, named first in the list of the Twelve

pace.did: He asked to be called out onto the water, and on the one word stepped down from the boat.
Told it was the Lord on the shore, he pulled his coat on and threw himself into the sea.
He drew a sword in the garden and struck the high priest's servant.

voice.did: Asked who the disciples said Jesus was, he was the one who answered.
voice.quote: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.

voice.did: He took Jesus aside and began to rebuke Him for what He had just said.
On the mountain he proposed building three tents.
He stood up with the eleven and addressed the crowd at Jerusalem.

lead.did: He stood up in the middle of about a hundred and twenty disciples and spoke.
He said he was going fishing and the others went with him.

conflict.did: He charged Ananias to his face with keeping back part of the price and lying to God.
He told Simon that his silver would perish with him, that he had no part in the matter, and told him to repent.
conflict.quote: May your silver perish with you

conflict.did: When those of the circumcision contended with him he explained what had happened in order.

doubt.did: He refused the vision's instruction, saying he had never eaten anything common or unclean.
He asked how many times he had to forgive and proposed a number.
He left the boat on a single word.

plan.did: He said he was going fishing, and they went out that night and caught nothing.

figures.name: Paul
figures.who: Pharisee of Tarsus, tentmaker, apostle to the nations

pace.did: After the night vision the party immediately looked for a way over to Macedonia.
He went into Arabia and back to Damascus and let three years pass before going up to Jerusalem.

voice.did: He reasoned in the synagogue and in the marketplace every day with those who met him.
He opposed Peter in public at Antioch.
voice.quote: I resisted him to his face

lead.did: He picked Silas and set out on his own circuit.
He fixed the party's route past Ephesus to reach Jerusalem by Pentecost.

conflict.did: The contention over Mark grew so sharp that he and Barnabas separated from each other.
conflict.quote: the contention grew so sharp that they separated from each other

conflict.did: He resisted Peter to his face at Antioch.

doubt.did: The text does not show this.

plan.did: He had settled the sailing route in advance so as not to spend time in Asia.
He wrote ahead about a journey to Spain and about being helped on his way by the Romans.

figures.name: Gideon
figures.who: son of Joash of Ophrah, called from the wine press to fight Midian

pace.did: He took ten of his servants and pulled down the altar by night rather than by day, because he feared his father’s household and the men of the city.

voice.did: He asked why all this had happened to them if the LORD was with them, and where His wondrous works were.
He said his family was the poorest in Manasseh and he was the least in his father’s house.

lead.did: He blew a trumpet, and Abiezer was gathered together to follow him.
He told the three hundred to watch him and do likewise, and to do as he did when he came to the outermost part of the camp.
When the men of Israel asked him to rule over them he said he would not rule over them, nor would his son.

conflict.did: He took the elders of Succoth and taught the men of the city with thorns and briers, and broke down the tower of Penuel.
When the men of Ephraim rebuked him sharply he answered them by comparing their gleaning with his vintage, and their anger was abated towards him.

doubt.did: He asked for a sign that it was really the one speaking with him.
doubt.quote: show me a sign that it is you who talk with me

doubt.did: He put a fleece on the threshing floor and asked for dew on it alone, then asked once more for the reverse.

plan.did: He was beating out wheat in the wine press, to hide it from the Midianites.
He divided the three hundred into three companies and put trumpets and empty pitchers with torches inside them into the hands of all of them.

figures.name: Deborah
figures.who: prophetess who judged Israel and summoned Barak against Sisera

pace.did: The text does not show this.

voice.did: She told Barak the mountain, the tribes, the number of men and where Sisera would be drawn.
She and Barak sang on that day.

lead.did: She judged Israel under the palm tree between Ramah and Bethel, and the children of Israel came up to her for judgement.
She told Barak to go down, and ten thousand men went after him.
lead.quote: Go; for this is the day

conflict.did: When Barak said he would go only if she went, she said she would go, and told him the journey would not be for his honour.

doubt.did: The text does not show this.

plan.did: The text does not show this.

figures.name: Esther
figures.who: Jewish orphan raised by Mordecai, made queen of Persia

pace.did: She called a three-day fast before going in to the king.
At the first banquet she asked the king and Haman to come to a second banquet the next day.

voice.did: She did not tell anyone in the palace who her people were, because Mordecai had told her not to.
voice.quote: Esther had not made known her people nor her relatives

voice.did: After she was made queen she still had not made it known, as Mordecai had commanded her.
At the second banquet she told the king to his face that she and her people had been sold to be destroyed.

lead.did: She ordered the fast in Susa and Mordecai did everything she had commanded him.
She asked the king to have letters written reversing Haman's.

conflict.did: She named Haman as the enemy while he was sitting at the table.
conflict.quote: An adversary and an enemy, even this wicked Haman!

conflict.did: She asked for the decree in Susa to run a further day.

doubt.did: She set out the law about the inner court and said she had not been called these thirty days.

plan.did: She prepared one banquet, then a second, and made her request only at the second.
She fixed the three days of fasting for herself, her maidens and the Jews of Susa first.

figures.name: Ruth
figures.who: Moabite widow who went with Naomi to Bethlehem

pace.did: She proposed going out to glean and went that day.
She went down to the threshing floor and did everything she had been told.

voice.did: She told Naomi to her face not to urge her to leave or to turn back from following her.

lead.did: She carried the barley into the city and gave Naomi what she had left over from her own meal.
She told Naomi that where she went she would go, and that her people would be her people.
Told that Boaz would say what she should do, she told him who she was and asked him to spread the corner of his garment over her.

conflict.did: The text does not show this.

doubt.did: She answered Naomi's instruction about the threshing floor by saying she would do all that she said.
doubt.quote: All that you say, I will do.

plan.did: The text does not show this.

figures.name: Hannah
figures.who: wife of Elkanah of Ramathaim, mother of Samuel

pace.did: She stayed behind from the yearly journey and waited until the child was weaned before bringing him.

voice.did: She prayed at the doorpost without making a sound.
voice.quote: Hannah spoke in her heart. Only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard.

voice.did: When she had brought Samuel up she prayed and said her song.

lead.did: The text does not show this.

conflict.did: The text does not show this.

doubt.did: After Eli's word she went her way and ate, and her face was no longer sad.

plan.did: She brought three bulls, an ephah of meal and a container of wine with the child.
She made him a little robe and brought it up to him year after year.

figures.name: Abigail
figures.who: wife of Nabal of Carmel, later wife of David

pace.did: She hurried and took bread, wine, sheep, grain, raisins and figs, and laid them on donkeys.
pace.quote: Then Abigail hurried and took two hundred loaves of bread

pace.did: She got down off the donkey as soon as she saw David and went to the ground in front of him.

voice.did: She asked David to hear her and then made her whole case to him.
She told Nabal nothing about it until the next morning.

lead.did: She sent her young men on before her and came after them.

conflict.did: She put herself between David's four hundred men and her husband's household and took the blame on herself.

doubt.did: The text does not show this.

plan.did: She gathered and loaded a full train of provisions before setting out to meet David.

figures.name: Rahab
figures.who: of Jericho, a prostitute whose house stood on the city wall, who hid Joshua's two spies

pace.did: She took the two men and hid them, and told the messengers she did not know where they came from.
She let them down by a cord through the window, for her house was on the wall.

voice.did: She told the king's messengers the men had gone out at dark and to pursue them quickly.
She told the two spies what the city had heard about the Red Sea and about Sihon and Og.

lead.did: She told the spies where to go and how many days to stay hidden.
She required an oath from them for her father, mother, brothers and sisters before they left.

conflict.did: The text does not show this.

doubt.did: The text does not show this.

plan.did: Two men came to her house and she hid them under the stalks of flax on the roof when the messengers came.

figures.name: Mary the mother of Jesus
figures.who: of Nazareth, betrothed to Joseph; at the wedding in Cana, at the cross, and with the disciples in Jerusalem

pace.did: At the greeting she was greatly troubled, and considered what kind of salutation it might be.
She got up in those days and went into the hill country in haste.

voice.did: After the shepherds came she kept what was said to herself and turned it over.
voice.quote: Mary kept all these sayings, pondering them in her heart.

voice.did: After Jerusalem she again kept what had been said in her heart.
She answered Elizabeth at length, saying that her soul magnified the Lord and her spirit had rejoiced in God her Saviour.
voice.quote: My soul magnifies the Lord.

lead.did: At the wedding she told the servants to do whatever He told them.
lead.quote: Whatever he says to you, do it.

lead.did: When the wine ran out she was the one who raised it, and she raised it with Him.

conflict.did: When they found Him in the temple she asked Him why He had treated them this way, and said that she and His father had been anxiously looking for Him.
conflict.quote: Son, why have you treated us this way?

doubt.did: She asked how what she had been told could happen.
doubt.quote: How can this be, seeing I am a virgin?

doubt.did: When they found Him in the temple she asked Him why He had treated them this way.
Once the angel had answered her she said she was the Lord's servant and asked that it be done to her according to His word.
doubt.quote: Behold, the servant of the Lord; let it be done to me according to your word.

plan.did: The text does not show this.

figures.name: Martha
figures.who: of Bethany, sister of Mary and Lazarus, who received Jesus into her house

pace.did: Hearing Jesus was coming she went out and met Him while her sister stayed in the house.

voice.did: She took her complaint about her sister to Jesus.
At the tomb she said out loud what four days would have done to the body.
voice.quote: Lord, by this time there is a stench, for he has been dead four days.

voice.did: She went and called her sister secretly to say that the Teacher was there and was calling her.

lead.did: She was the one who received Him into the house.

conflict.did: She asked Jesus to tell her sister to come and help her.
When He arrived she told Him that if He had been there her brother would not have died.
conflict.quote: Lord, if you would have been here, my brother wouldn’t have died.

doubt.did: Told to take away the stone, she objected first that he had been dead four days.

plan.did: The text does not show this.

figures.name: Mary Magdalene
figures.who: of Magdala, out of whom seven demons had gone, first at the empty tomb

pace.did: She went to the tomb early, while it was still dark.
Seeing the stone moved she ran to Simon Peter and the other disciple.
pace.quote: she ran and came to Simon Peter

voice.did: She went to the disciples and told them what she had seen and what had been said to her.
Asked why she was weeping, she said plainly that the body had been taken and she did not know where.

lead.did: She went with Him and the Twelve through the cities and villages, among the women who served them from their possessions.
Mark names her among the women who had followed Him and served Him when He was in Galilee.

conflict.did: The text does not show this.

doubt.did: The text does not show this.

plan.did: When the Sabbath was past she bought spices with the other women to go and anoint Him.
plan.quote: bought spices, that they might come and anoint him

figures.name: Barnabas
figures.who: Levite of Cyprus, sent by the church in Jerusalem to Antioch, Paul’s travelling companion

pace.did: When he and Paul heard what the crowd at Lystra was doing, they tore their clothes and sprang into the multitude, crying out.

voice.did: When he came to Antioch and saw the grace of God he was glad, and exhorted them all to remain near to the Lord.
He and Paul reported to the gathered assembly what God had done among the nations, and the multitude listened.

lead.did: When the disciples in Jerusalem were afraid of Saul, he took him and brought him to the apostles and told them what had happened on the road.
He went to Tarsus to look for Saul, found him and brought him to Antioch, and for a whole year they taught many people there.

conflict.did: He and Paul had no small discord and discussion with those who were teaching the brothers at Antioch.
He planned to take Mark with them; when Paul did not agree the contention grew sharp and they separated, and he took Mark and sailed to Cyprus.

doubt.did: The text does not show this.

plan.did: Having a field, he sold it, brought the money and laid it at the apostles’ feet.

figures.name: Jesus
figures.who: of Nazareth, Whose acts here are taken only from the four Gospels

pace.did: Moved with compassion, He stretched out His hand, touched the leper and said He wanted to, and the leprosy left him.
He went out to the mountain to pray and continued all night in prayer to God; when it was day He called His disciples and chose twelve of them.

voice.did: Questioned by the high priest He said His teaching had all been done in public.
voice.quote: I spoke openly to the world.

voice.did: He spoke to them openly, and Peter took Him and began to rebuke Him.
voice.quote: He spoke to them openly.

voice.did: Before Pilate He made no further answer, so that Pilate marvelled.
voice.quote: But Jesus made no further answer, so that Pilate marvelled.

lead.did: On the road up to Jerusalem He walked ahead of the Twelve and they followed.
lead.quote: Jesus was going in front of them

lead.did: He told Simon and Andrew to come after Him, and said He would make them fishers for men.
lead.quote: I will make you into fishers for men.

lead.did: He went up the mountain, called to Himself those whom He wanted, and appointed twelve to be with Him and to be sent out to preach.
At supper He took a towel and a basin and washed the disciples' feet, then told them that He, their Lord and Teacher, had given them an example to follow.
He called the Twelve and began to send them out two by two, and gave them authority over unclean spirits.

conflict.did: He made a whip of cords, drove all out of the temple with the sheep and the oxen, poured out the money of the changers and overthrew their tables.
When one of those with Him cut off the ear of the high priest's servant at the arrest, He touched the man's ear and healed him.
He asked Peter three times whether he loved Him, and each time told him to feed or tend His sheep.

doubt.did: The Gospels record Him asking questions among the teachers (Luke 2:46) and yielding to the Father's will in the garden (Matthew 26:42), and they also say He knew what was coming (John 18:4). Neither end of this axis describes that, so He is not placed on it.

plan.did: He sent two disciples with instructions about a man with a pitcher and an upper room, and they found it as He had said.
Near Jerusalem He sent two disciples into a village for a young donkey, telling them where it would be tied and what to say if anyone asked.
On the way to Jairus's house He stopped in the crowd, asked who had touched His clothes, and stayed until the woman had told Him all the truth.

figures.name: Judith
figures.who: widow of Manasses of Bethulia, who went with her maid into the camp of Holofernes

pace.did: She told the rulers to stand at the gate that night, and said she would go out with her maid.
pace.quote: You shall all stand at the gate tonight. I will go out with my maid.

voice.did: When the rulers of Bethulia came to her, she told them that what they had said before the people that day was not right.
voice.quote: your word that you have spoken before the people this day is not right

voice.did: She said with a loud voice that God had destroyed their enemies by her hand that night, then took the head out of the bag and showed it.
voice.quote: She said to them with a loud voice

voice.did: She told the rulers not to enquire about her act, and that she would not tell them until the things she would do were finished.
voice.quote: I will not tell you until the things are finished that I will do

lead.did: She told the people to hang the head on the battlement of their wall, and at sunrise to take up their weapons, send every valiant man out of the city and set a captain over them.
lead.quote: take this head, and hang it upon the battlement of your wall

lead.did: At the gate she told Ozias and the elders standing by it to command that it be opened for her, and they commanded the young men to open it.
She went before all the people in the dance, leading all the women, and all the men of Israel followed in their armour.
lead.quote: she went before all the people in the dance, leading all the women

conflict.did: She asked the rulers who they were, that they had tested God that day and stood in the place of God amongst men.
conflict.quote: Now who are you that you have tested God this day

conflict.did: She took Holofernes' sword down from the bedpost at his head, took hold of his hair, and struck twice upon his neck.
conflict.quote: She struck twice upon his neck with all her might and cut off his head

doubt.did: The text does not show this.

plan.did: She gave her maid a container of wine and a flask of oil, filled a bag with roasted grain, figs and bread, and packed all her vessels together.
plan.quote: filled a bag with roasted grain, lumps of figs, and fine bread

plan.did: She had told her servant to stand outside her bedchamber and wait for her to come out, as she did daily, and she spoke to Bagoas in the same words.
She distributed her goods before she died, to her husband's nearest kin and to her own.
plan.quote: She distributed her goods before she died

figures.name: Tobit
figures.who: Israelite of the tribe of Naphtali carried captive to Nineveh, father of Tobias, blind for eight years

pace.did: Told that one of his people had been strangled and cast out in the marketplace, he sprang up before he had tasted anything and took him up into a chamber until sunset.
pace.quote: Before I had tasted anything, I sprang up

pace.did: When he knew that he was being sought to be put to death, he withdrew himself for fear.

voice.did: He wept and prayed in his sorrow, and asked that his spirit be taken from him.
voice.quote: Command my spirit to be taken from me, that I may be released

voice.did: Grown very old, he called his son with his son's six sons and told him he was ready to depart out of this life.
He buried privately those whom King Sennacherib killed; the king sought for the bodies and they were not found.
voice.quote: I buried them privately

lead.did: Seeing an abundance of meat, he told his son to go and bring whatever poor man of their kindred he could find, and said he would wait for him.
He gave his son the handwriting, told him to seek a man to go with him and said he would give the man wages.
lead.quote: Seek a man who will go with you, and I will give him wages

conflict.did: When the kid began to cry in his house, he asked his wife where it had come from and whether it was stolen, and told her to give it back to the owners.
conflict.quote: Where did this kid come from? Is it stolen? Give it back to the owners

conflict.did: He welcomed the man as a brother and asked him not to be angry that he had sought to know his tribe and family.
conflict.quote: because I sought to know your tribe and family

conflict.did: When his wife wept and asked why he had sent their child away, he told her not to worry and that the boy would return safe and sound, and she stopped weeping.

doubt.did: Told that his son had found someone to go with him, he said to call the man to him so that he might know his tribe and whether he was trustworthy.
doubt.quote: Call him to me, that I may know of what tribe he is, and whether he be a trustworthy man to go with you.

doubt.did: He asked the man his tribe and family, and when the man answered with a question of his own he said that he wanted to know his kindred and his name.
doubt.quote: I want to know, brother, your kindred and your name.

doubt.did: When his wife said the kid had been given to her as a gift on top of her wages, he did not believe her and asked her to return it to the owners.
doubt.quote: I didn’t believe her, and I asked her to return it to the owners

plan.did: On a journey into Media he left ten talents of silver in trust with Gabael at Rages.
Having asked for death, he remembered the money left in trust and said to himself that he should call his son and explain about it before he died.
plan.quote: why do I not call my son Tobias, that I may explain to him about the money before I die?

plan.did: He had sat down to a good dinner at the feast of Pentecost; when news came that one of his people lay strangled in the marketplace he left it untasted and took the man up into a chamber.
